prompt.en: Which word is a possessive pronoun?

stages.choice_rule: Build four unique lowercase words. Exactly one is a possessive pronoun from mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Take the other three from the stem: prefer a possessive adjective (my, your, her, our, their), a personal pronoun (i, me, you, he, him, she, we, us, they, them), or the owned noun. Never two possessive pronouns. Never its as the answer. Never a noun with 's. Shuffle so the answer is not always first.

gold_items.stem: She said the cookie is hers.
We know the kite is ours.
They think the cat is theirs.
This is their cake, not ours.

roots: Every stem is one kid-world sentence with exactly one possessive pronoun used alone after a linking verb or after not/or (the ball is mine; not yours).
Correct answers may be only mine, yours, his, hers, ours, or theirs. Never its. Never my, your, her, our, their. Never a noun with 's.
Use his as the answer only in a stand-alone slot (is his, are his). Never his hat.
Wrong choices must come from the stem. On tier 2 include a personal pronoun. On tier 3 include a possessive adjective in the stem and as a choice.
Spread mine, yours, his, hers, ours, and theirs across the pool. Use <NAME> for people. No brands.

tier_rules.1: Stems of four to six words. The pronoun follows is or are. Distractors are the noun, the, is, or this. Add a lemma picture of the noun.
tier_rules.2: Stems of five to seven words. Add a personal pronoun (she, we, they) as a trap. Use two-syllable kid nouns such as cookie, puppy, or kite.
tier_rules.3: Stems of six to ten words. Put a possessive adjective (my, your, her, our, their) in the same stem as the pronoun so that adjective is the main trap.
